item: Comprehensions under a lock or a finally are functions of their own in four functions, so an interrupt cannot skip the release (R205)
summary: On CPython 3.13 a comprehension is inlined into its function and its filter-skip back-edge sits outside the exception table of the with/finally around it, so a KeyboardInterrupt delivered there skips the cleanup (measured on a minimal case: 12,283 of 12,491 interrupts). The tree-wide read-only scan (/mnt/project-files/audit-0.5.0/inputs/comprehensions-in-try-report.md) found 100 such comprehensions in 68 functions under a with/finally/except BaseException; this moves the Tier A sites with a plausible chain to boot or a CLI into small functions of their own, body unchanged: upgrade_sources_to_composite_key (four comprehensions between the try and the BEGIN; the finally turns foreign-key enforcement back on; reached from init_db), DamageRegistry.confirmed_damage (two, under self._lock), lane_engine (one, under the module _lock) and dispose_lane (one, under the same lock; the bare-name scan missed its chain, which the Opus read found through the aliased import in encrypt_tool.py, scripts/encrypt_db.py -> encrypt_all -> dispose_all). tests/test_r205_comprehensions_under_cleanup.py reads the compiled code with the dis helper of test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py and is red with the old code (3 failed). Reachability in the report is by bare function name, depth 4, a hint and not a proof; Left as audit items: Tier A scripts/fault_harness.py run_scenario and run_contention_zip (a test harness, not product code), the two Tier A unconfirmed (geo/osm_downloads.py list, monitoring/storage_events.py update), Tier B (31 worker-only or unreached functions) and Tier C (30 session or file closes that process exit reclaims).
